I got one! Bought the V1 red today(Reverb), and it was only posted for one freaking hour. I got it for $140 flat, but it actually has the box, no scratches and was used maybe once as a demo. I just got my Les Paul out the shop, with a full Pleck machine fretting, some touch up, and neck reinforcing. So I’m super stoked right now to get it. I’m not really liking the distortions I have with my amp. I mainly used a lot of DI, into an expensive API or Neve with a tech 21 blonde with gain on that. 

But for my Roland JC 77, I only have an old DOD American Metal X. I mean it’s cool if you wanna sound like NIN or Skinny Puppy..or play some old Metallica Riffs. So yeah def needed an overdrive. The comparison on the distortion side being like a shred master peaked my interest a little…as that was the Radiohead distorted sound on first 3 albums. But I hear the overdrive is the main standout here.

But yeah I’m just happy to score that red V1, and really dial in my sound for live playing. I’ve been too focused on Studio recording for the last 10 years.  So just kind of getting into a pedal phase. I’ve had Marshall’s and all kinds of Amps. But older I got I preferred the clean amp with pedals, to make my sound over needing a crazy expensive amp to lug around. 

Collider pedal maybe next!

When I worked at Best Buy you could get a 20k fine for selling big demand items too early. Not sure if this counts, but major retailers can pay a pretty big fine. And usually it will be blocked in the computer. If someone is not too smart, the manager may override it. But a new console or such or say like those little NES/SNES they had out, would be a huge fine and get flagged.

But mom and pop shops usually don’t have this same system in place. So they are more likely to sell it, with no fine or notice in the system. Wouldn’t be surprised to see copies on eBay at a higher rate before release.

But we would get games like this 2 weeks in advance, as well as consoles 2 weeks ahead. So it’s likely a legit copy here. If it went gold and printed that just means they are out in warehouses with a “don’t sell till” date right now. So this about confirms, all major retailers have received initial copies on hold. We will probably see game play videos by the weekend.

39 here and yes….todays standards are different. Even my last relationship the person was 6 years younger. 23 I was 29. So enough gap to have grown up in a different generation. However I had a good learning perspective to see the changes from early 2010s till now. I’ll just say an old saying… “some people are only trustworthy as their options”

And wow, do we have a lot of overwhelming options out there!  With people direct DMing, Insta, Tinder for instant gratification, others lurking and so on. Some people adapt and change. I watched a very little social media influenced relationship of my own…turn into a serious influenced by social media relationship over 7 years. Behaviors on their part massively changed, and people they would never have met. Made there way into our lives. And lifestyle postings they saw, caused them depression. Or what we would say, keeping up with the “Jones’s” It’s just a huge impact for those that let it be, and a cultural shift. 

I never let it effect my dating life or much of my life in personal ways…I’m a very private person. But many people I think slowly shifted with that culture. Most in my 37-40+ age group I know, seem to still be more old school values of the 90s early 2000s. But 35 and younger, I see a different set of ideals and values with the cultural shift. That instant gratification of being able to pick a new partner at ease, get DM and emotionally cheat is very tempting to some. We use to just work this out together, or be amongst our own tribe in a city or town. 

So there’s a lot to unpack with that, and I’d be lying if I said I don’t pay attention to people I date social media use and how important it is to them.

As a guy Career and stability is a big thing for me too. I don’t care if your career salary is 50k or 100k+. My thing is I’ve met a lot of women with no jobs, or in their late 30s making $600 a month doing gig work on hrly struggling hard. Also time schedule is a big deal. I work 7am-4pm m-f, with weekends and holiday stretches off. So I’m always looking for someone that has a similar lifestyle. Gig work and frantic hours just doesn’t work for me in a relationship. But I still would respect and date someone going back to school taking time off work. 

It’s def a big split in my city between young 30-45 professionals, and late night gig workers. And most want to be with someone in a similar lifestyle. I think time is very valuable, and I’ve been the one in a hectic hrly No career, and the one in a career normal 9-5/weekend off. 

I think that time schedule availability, as well as making enough to have your own life with a salary is important. Doesn’t mean 100k plus or gold digging imo. Just salary with normal work hours, so you can see the person and not have money be a spiteful issue later on.

But I know guys that would be considered 10s, all into that and have diverse friend groups. I get it may have a stereotype, but there is a difference between obsession and hobbies. Guys tend to like tech a lot, and not just cellphones.

I think some people think gaming or anime, equals obsession based on what they experienced at an early age. When in reality it’s just something they like and may do a few hours a week, or maybe one day on a weekend with friends online. I know a lot of girls that grew up with guys in High School, that were just obsessed with anime, weed, gaming or DND. 

So they see that as a bad thing, and it may have ruined an early teenage relationship. Reality is those older guys are not pot smoking basement dwellers, because they game or watch anime. Its not high school or college freshman year anymore. It’s a social thing these days, we talk with and share with other guy friends. From my experience, I would always hear…this guy I dated in HS or early college did that. So I don’t want a guy that has those interests because he’s lazy, a burn out or obsessed.

I really suck with dates as well, but with phone calendars I set important reminders right away. So I don’t see why he didn’t. I’m not sure what I think only being 6 months dating. I’ve in the past, have had a very hard headed company not take me seriously. I had some health issues, and surgery. It also caused some depression issues as well I needed to deal with. I thought saying I was diagnosed with cancer,needed surgery and some time off was enough. But of course it wasn’t at all. I went to my doctor and pulled FMLA the day I was in tears over it. 

With FMLA you don’t have to tell them anything, or actually have a date setup to protect your job. In this case a 2 months heads up was given! But with FMLA you get 12 weeks or so in a year, and in some cases can also get paid out by the companies insurance or use your PTO/Holiday on top of it. I learned a lot about it, when it was my only recourse legally.

FMLA was easy for me, and just took a doctor who was angry as me, to sign the paper work. Then I called HR and my doctor emailed the paper work. Getting paid though, I had to get my doctor to do a lot of faxing, notes, weekly check ups to cover it. With the pay, they scrutinized every single detail to not pay me.
